lineas.texto: Part two. Every afternoon, you train in the castle yard.
You swing a wooden sword at a post in the ground. Again, and again, and again.
Your practice sword is heavier than a real one, so the real one will feel light.
Then you visit the smith. Every time his hammer falls, the sparks fly.
He is making a horseshoe. He dips it in water, and it hisses like a snake.
A coat of mail can take weeks of work. That is why it is worth so much.
At night, the great hall fills with music, laughter, and woodsmoke.
You fall asleep by the fire, your arms still aching.
Part three, {when_next}: the day you become a knight.
